content:
The Treaty of Tordesillas was negotiated after Columbus’s 1492 voyage, which Spain knew opened access to new lands west of the Atlantic. Portugal already had established interests along the African coast and route to India. Spain wanted to secure rights to these newly encountered western lands without Portuguese interference.  

Option (A) is unrelated — the Barbary states were in North Africa, not relevant to the line’s placement.  
Option (B) is unlikely — Portugal knew of Columbus’s discovery, hence the need for a treaty.  
Option (C) is incorrect — Spain did not seek to preserve Native states’ independence; they sought conquest and conversion.  
Option (D) fits — Spain accepted the line because they believed the lands west (the Americas) were easier to claim and control than the eastern lands (India and East Indies), where Portugal had the advantage.  

Final answer: (D)
